questions.question: Select the management function that involves assigning duties to catering staff. a). Advertising b). Auditing c). Recruitment d). Organizing / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Moist-heat cooking methods
  • These methods use water, steam or another aqueous liquid to transfer heat.
  • • Boiling: Food is cooked in water at its boiling point. Example: rice, eggs and vegetables.
  • • Simmering: Food is cooked gently in liquid below the boiling point. Example: soups and
  • gravies.
  • • Steaming: Food is cooked using steam. Example: idli and steamed vegetables.
  • • Poaching: Food is cooked gently in liquid at a relatively low temperature. Example: eggs.
  • • Blanching: Food is briefly treated with boiling water or steam before further processing.
  • Advantages: Moist-heat methods can produce tender foods and are useful for preparing large
  • quantities.

questions.solution_html:
• Dry-heat cooking methods
  • These methods use hot air, hot surfaces, fat or direct radiant heat.
  • • Baking: Food is cooked using hot air in an oven. Example: bread and cakes.
  • • Roasting: Food is cooked using dry heat. Example: roasted meat and vegetables.
  • • Grilling: Food is cooked using direct heat from above or below. Example: grilled
  • chicken.
  • • Shallow frying: Food is cooked in a small quantity of oil.
  • • Deep frying: Food is immersed in hot oil. Example: samosas and cutlets.
  • • Sautéing: Food is cooked quickly in a small amount of fat.
  • Advantages: Dry-heat methods can produce desirable browning, crispness, flavour and texture.

questions.solution_html:
• Combination cooking methods
  • These methods combine dry heat and moist heat.
  • • Braising: Food is first browned and then cooked slowly with a small quantity of liquid.
  • Example: braised meat.
  • • Stewing: Small pieces of food are cooked slowly in liquid. Example: meat stew.
  • • Pot roasting: Food is initially browned and then cooked in a covered vessel with limited
  • liquid.
  • Advantages: Combination methods improve tenderness, develop flavour and are suitable for
  • preparing many meat and vegetable dishes.

questions.question: Explain the methods used for maintaining inventory records in railway food service operations. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Methods used for maintaining inventory records in railway food service operations
  • • Stock registers: Record the quantity of food items received, issued and remaining.
  • • Bin cards: Track the movement and balance of individual items in storage.
  • • Purchase and issue records: Maintain details of purchased ingredients and items issued to
  • the kitchen.
  • • Stock verification: Conduct regular physical checks and compare actual stock with
  • recorded stock.
  • • FIFO/FEFO: Use First -In, First -Out or First-Expired, First -Out to manage stock and
  • reduce spoilage.
  • • Digital inventory systems: Use computerized records to monitor stock levels, expiry dates
  • and reorder requirements.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Describe the different food preservation methods used in railway catering. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Different food preservation methods used in railway catering
  • • Refrigeration: Slows microbial growth and extends the storage life of perishable foods.
  • • Freezing: Preserves foods by lowering their temperature and restricting microbial growth.
  • • Heat treatment: Cooking and pasteurization destroy many harmful microorganisms.
  • • Canning: Uses heat processing and airtight packaging to preserve suitable foods.
  • • Dehydration: Removes moisture to reduce microbial growth.
  • • Chemical preservation: Approved preservatives help control spoilage in suitable food
  • products.
  • • Packaging: Airtight and appropria te food -grade packaging protects food from
  • contamination.

questions.question: Describe the different types of food service operations available in railways. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Different types of food service operations available in railways
  • • Pantry car service: Food is prepared or handled in designated onboard facilities and
  • served to passengers.
  • • Onboard catering: Meals and refreshments are supplied directly to passengers during the
  • journey.
  • • E-catering: Passengers order food through digital platforms for delivery at designated
  • stations.
  • • Station food outlets: Restaurants, food courts and stalls provide meals and snacks.
  • • Refreshment rooms: Provide food and beverages to passengers at railway stations.
  • • Packaged food service: Ready -to-eat meals, snacks and beverages are supplied for
  • convenient consumption.
